name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt the 3px focus ring at 7:1 contrast. This meets WCAG 2.2 AAA for visibility and works on all devices, including high-DPI screens. The trade-off is slightly more space used in tight layouts, but clarity for keyboard users outweighs that.

name: Reader
text: The 3px ring at 7:1 still fails users who need *both* high contrast *and* reduced motion—7:1 is too harsh for some low-vision users with light sensitivity, and 3px is too thin for those with motor control issues. A 4px ring at 6:1 keeps clarity without triggering motion discomfort, and testing with real screen-reader users on high-DPI devices settles it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 4px focus ring at 6:1 contrast. This balances visibility for keyboard users with comfort for those sensitive to harsh contrasts or motion, meeting WCAG 2.1 AA while avoiding the extremes of 3px/7:1. The trade-off is slightly less crisp focus visibility in bright conditions, but it covers more user needs without excluding anyone.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-5424, worker-5454, worker-7342 — done, dissolved]

name: Reader
text: The 4px ring at 6:1 still risks blending into busy backgrounds on mobile—users with tremor or glare sensitivity may lose sight of focus entirely. A 5px ring at 5:1 keeps the ring visible *and* reduces harsh contrast while staying within WCAG 2.1 AA. Test with 10 low-vision users on both light and dark modes to settle it.
